correctness.rationale: The source H-description gives every proper binary-building-set facet, and orthogonal projection into the fixed-sum affine hull gives exact facet-normal length sqrt(|I|(m-|I|)/m). Any frontier partitions the ground set, so summing normalized clearance inequalities gives the stated upper bound. Conversely, the laminar inclusion tree admits a recursive minimum-mass allocation: the required mass at each node is the maximum of its own shifted lower bound and the sum of the child requirements. The root requirement is exactly the maximum shifted weight over all frontiers, so the minimum frontier ratio is feasible. This proves both the inradius and the complete incenter system.

value.rationale: Fertilitopes are a natural recent polytope family introduced to organize stack-sorting fertility phenomena and classified as integral binary nestohedra. The theorem determines a standard Euclidean invariant for every connected member and replaces a continuous Chebyshev-center optimization with a finite combinatorial frontier minimum on the binary building-set tree. The accompanying complete incenter description also exposes when optimal centers can be nonunique, making the result a structural metric complement to the established face, lattice-point, and Ehrhart theory.
